newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway c.bank chief sees moderate Europe inflation.
newsitem.headline: Norway c.bank chief sees moderate Europe inflation.

text.p: Norwegian central bank governor Kjell Storvik said on Thursday he expected inflation to stay moderate in western Europe in the forseeable future.
In a speech in Oslo, Storvik said countries should pursue tight fiscal policies in the long term because of high budget deficits and big debts.
"I am not among those who believe inflation is dead, but there is reason to believe that inflation will stay relatively moderare in the forseeable future in western Europe," he said.
"In the short term there is a lot of free production capacity in the economies."
He said increased competition in many countries also was leading to lower price growth.
Checking inflation had been given a greater role in economic policies, he said.
"At the same time many central banks have been given clear inflation targets and means to reach these goals," Storvik said.
